generation.difference: The first complete installation attempt in the Agent-created fresh environment used torch 2.1.2 and x86_64 CUDA wheels and was not the final program. The Agent retained the same fresh environment, repaired network and build-isolation failures, replaced the mismatched binaries with ARM wheels, upgraded to CPU torch 2.7.1, and observed zero missing imports before submission. The consolidated final program was first executed exactly from a clean checkout during post-session qualification.

repair_tags.observation: Two conda environment attempts failed while downloading Anaconda metadata, after which the Agent switched to a uv-managed Python 3.10 environment.

During construction and the first voluntary replay, the Agent installed x86_64 causal-conv1d and mamba-ssm shared objects into an ARM64 environment to make static imports resolvable. It later replaced these with aarch64 wheels before submission.

In the Agent-visible fresh environment after applying the final package choices, torch was 2.7.1+cpu with torch.version.cuda=None and torch.cuda.is_available()=False. Direct imports of the ARM causal_conv1d_cuda and selective_scan_cuda extensions failed because libcudart.so.12 and libc10_cuda.so were unavailable. Exact post-session qualification and Official checked the EnvBench missing-import goal but did not execute these runtime imports.
The submitted program installs flash-attn 2.5.9.post1 with FLASH_ATTENTION_SKIP_CUDA_BUILD=TRUE, which installs its Python layer without compiling the CUDA extension.
Each exact independent replay downloaded 196.3 MB and 533.3 MB ARM wheels from GitHub in addition to the ordinary dependency set; qualification and Official took about nine minutes each.

scientific_interpretation.reason: The unrestricted strong Agent used one voluntary fresh environment to expose and repair several installation defects, submitted a complete program, and then passed exact independent qualification and Official. The fact that the submitted environment still lacks a usable CUDA runtime is a path-quality finding under the Official-primary adjudication, not an EnvBench failure or evidence that automatic replay beats this control.
scientific_interpretation.measurement_implication: Zero missing imports can coexist with unusable compiled-extension imports. Official Pass@1 and runtime completeness must remain separate axes if deployment quality is analyzed beyond the leaderboard objective.
scientific_interpretation.live_frontier_implication: No promotion evidence; terminal Official success was achieved without frontier management.
